_source_note: Real Synthea-generated patient (Agnes294 Wuckert783). Her generated record has a real Osteoarthritis of knee condition but NO documented physical therapy / conservative therapy encounters at all -- this claim demonstrates the trajectory tool correctly finding zero evidence (step_therapy_met=False because total_conservative_encounters=0), not a fabricated 'almost enough' duration.

Real Synthea-generated patient (Renaldo199 Crist667). His generated record has a real, verified Warfarin Sodium prescription (active, multiple refills through 2026) and a real Ciprofloxacin prescription on 2020-12-03 for a real Acute infective cystitis (UTI) diagnosis -- this claim demonstrates the drug interaction tool firing on a genuine warfarin + ciprofloxacin overlap in real generated data, not a hand-built fixture.

Real Synthea-generated patient (Eunice461 Fay398). Her generated record has a real Osteoarthritis of hip diagnosis (SNOMED 239872002) but, like CLM-2001, NO documented physical therapy / conservative therapy encounters. payer_name is set to exactly match the real CMS Medicare LCD policy data already indexed (POL-MEDICARE-LCD-34163 / L34163 'Total Hip Arthroplasty') rather than a commercial payer name -- this is the one claim in the sample set that actually resolves the payer_name exact-match gap flagged in the Backend Architecture docs, so this claim's policy match against the real Medicare hip LCD is the closest thing to a fully real, end-to-end (real patient + real policy + real decision) demo case available. ICD-10 code M16.9 (Osteoarthritis of hip, unspecified, unspecified hip) was chosen deliberately as the unspecified/no-laterality code since the underlying SNOMED data carries no laterality -- unlike CLM-2001's M17.11, which specifies a right knee that isn't actually present in that patient's coded data either (a pre-existing inconsistency in the current sample set worth knowing about, not fixed here since it wasn't asked for).

Real Synthea-generated patient (Galen747 Koelpin146). His generated record has a real, active Atrial fibrillation diagnosis (2023) managed with Warfarin Sodium 5mg (active) plus a real, separate history of Acute non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (2013) managed with an active aspirin 81mg prescription -- two independently legitimate prescriptions from what would likely be two different care episodes/prescribers, creating a real, undetected bleeding-risk interaction. Demonstrates the drug interaction tool catching a genuine overlap that arose from parallel, clinically-reasonable treatment tracks rather than an obviously erroneous prescription.

Real Synthea-generated patient (Chester802 Aufderhar910). His generated record has real, active Essential hypertension and Chronic congestive heart failure diagnoses, managed with concurrently active Lisinopril (ACE inhibitor) and Losartan Potassium (ARB) prescriptions -- a real dual renin-angiotensin-aldosterone-system (RAAS) blockade combination current guidelines generally advise against due to hyperkalemia/renal risk. Note: this patient's real generated record also shows two lisinopril entries (10mg and 20mg) both marked 'active' on the same date -- likely a Synthea dose-titration artifact rather than a genuine duplicate prescription, left as-is rather than silently cleaned up since it's real generated output.
